command.description: with `block`: the command whose output this is

cutOff.description: with `final`: the turn ended on this error (its agent reported it), so `text` is the answer as far as it got

agent.inbox.description: A terminal's agent integration takes the messages queued for it (agent.prompt to a target whose integration reports `protocol` ≥ 1) and delivers them to its agent, without touching the terminal. `ack` first drops the messages it delivered (`started`: that delivery started a new turn, so agent.wait now waits for that turn as after a prompt to an idle agent; otherwise it joined the running turn). Then it answers the messages waiting that no open connection holds, oldest first, each sender's name and each message's mentions resolved now; they are held by this connection until it acks them or closes, and offered again then. With `waitMs`, when none waits, it answers as soon as one arrives (at most that long, then with none). An integration acks a message once its agent has recorded it, never before, and dedupes by id (one comes again after a lost connection or a restart). Messages are saved with the board, so an app restart keeps them; when the agent session they were queued for ends first (agent.release, its integration dying, another session reported, the terminal deleted) they bounce, as agent.prompt says.

ack.description: messages this integration has handed to its agent

started.description: with `ack`: their delivery started a new turn (the agent was idle), rather than joining the running one

waitMs.description: wait this long for a message when none waits

agent.restart.description: Relaunch the agent in a terminal tile in place: the tile keeps its id, name, frame, and its agent's recorded model and thinking level (agent.report_session `model`, `thinking`). Its zmx session is killed (the agent and everything it started end) and a new session runs the relaunched command; a hosted terminal's (`props.host`) on its host, through that host's easld (`session.kill`, `session.spawn`), `unavailable` while easl isn't connected to it. `resume`: the tile's agent reopens its recorded session (omp `--resume=<session path>`, claude `--resume <id>`, codex `resume <id>`, gemini `--resume <id>`, opencode `--session <id>`), with the options of the tile's `command` when it runs that agent, and the recorded model and thinking (omp `--model=<model> --thinking=<level>`; they replace any the command gave); `unavailable` when no session is recorded (its agent never reported one, or it exited). `fresh`: the same command, model and thinking without a session (a session selector or prompt the command had is left out); a terminal with no recorded agent reruns its `command`. `args` are appended either way. Refused with `conflict` while another restart of the terminal runs or a prompt is being pasted into it (even with `force`: it would land in the relaunched agent), and unless `force` while the agent is `working` (restored or not) or `blocked`, has a prompt whose turn hasn't started (typed, or a message its integration delivered, within agent.wait's grace for it), has a message queued that its integration hasn't taken yet (agent.wait waits for it too; a forced restart bounces it), may hold a draft (agent.list `draft` true, or absent: its integration doesn't say), or the terminal has keyboard focus (agent.list `focused`: the user may be typing in it); checked again just before the kill. While it runs nothing else reaches the terminal: agent.prompt to it fails with `conflict`, and agent.inbox offers it nothing; a typed prompt whose agent session ended before its paste (the restart came while it read the screen) types nothing and fails `unavailable`. Nothing is relaunched until the old session is confirmed gone: when it can't be (another easl instance owns it, or it is still listed 3 s after the kill), `unavailable`, with the session, its agent and its queue as they were; a tile closed while its session is killed is `not_found`, with nothing relaunched. Killing the agent ends its session (agent.inbox): in either mode the messages still queued for it bounce, and none reaches the relaunched agent. The tile's `command` becomes the relaunched one without its session selector, so a reboot relaunches the same agent; its lifecycle is cleared (`unknown`) until the new agent reports, so agent.wait gives it 15 s for a first report. Only tiles of open boards; a remote board's terminal is its host's to restart, through the host's API.

target.description: a tile id, `name` or `name@board`, as agent.prompt's

caller.description: the asking terminal, whose board a bare `target` name is looked up on first; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

mode.description: resume: reopen the recorded session; fresh: a new session with the same command, model and thinking

args.description: arguments appended to the relaunched command, e.g. ["--plan"]

force.description: restart even though the agent is working or blocked, has a prompt whose turn hasn't started or a message queued it hasn't taken, the user is in the terminal, or its editor holds a draft (or may: its integration doesn't say): that work, prompt, dialog or draft is lost, and the queued messages bounce. Never past another restart of the terminal or a prompt being pasted into it

agent.description: the tile as relaunched: lifecycle `unknown` until its new agent reports

command.description: the argv the new session runs

follow.report.description: Report a file location an agent just read, edited, or wrote; re-aims that terminal's follow tile, creating it in a free spot near the terminal (unless the user is working in it, which holds re-aims for ~10 s). Ignored while the terminal's `props.follow` is false, and for files outside the board root, the terminal's cwd, and the other worktrees of their repositories (a worktree file keeps its absolute path and its own gutter), scratch files in the temp directory, missing files, images, PDFs, archives, and other binaries: the tile keeps its last real file.

path.description: absolute path or path relative to the board root

range.description: where to aim; omitted with `changes`, the hunk spanning the most lines (the last of equals)

changes.description: an edit's hunks as lines of the file now (a deletion: the line after it); the tile flashes them all

view.attention.description: Raise an attention marker pointing at an object (one per object; raising again replaces its message), or remove it with `clear: true`. A marker belongs to the caller's turn: raising one clears the markers the same caller raised in earlier turns (a turn starts when its lifecycle goes to working from idle, done, or no state; answering an approval, blocked → working, continues the turn); markers from this turn stay. The user seeing the object also clears it. Unseen markers are stored with the board and survive app restarts; deleting the object removes its marker. Never moves the user's viewport.

clear.description: remove this object's marker instead of raising it

caller.description: the raising agent's terminal; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

id.description: the marked object (markers are keyed by object)

active.description: a marker is showing after this call

cleared.description: present when raising cleared the caller's markers from earlier turns: their objects

view.get.description: What the user is looking at right now, without pixels: the visible board rect and zoom, the prompt-target terminal, the tile with keyboard focus, the selection, whether the window is visible on screen, and its appearance (dark or light).

promptTarget.description: terminal that receives the tray and dictation

visible.description: the window is at least partly visible on a displayed Space

appearance.description: the window's appearance, which tiles and renders draw in: match charts and pages to it (dark: transparent or dark backgrounds, light text)

view.open_url.description: Open a web address the way a ⌘-click on it in the caller's terminal does: an http or https URL shows in a browser tile beside the caller, and a tile already showing that address (compared by scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment, so `HTTP://Example.com:80` is `http://example.com/`) is reused (`existing: true`) instead of a duplicate. The user's view pans the least that shows the tile, never so far that the caller's terminal leaves view. Keyboard focus stays where it was: the tile is selected unless that would take the keyboard from another tile than a terminal (a note being edited, a page or code rows being typed in), which keeps it and its selection. Anything but http(s) is `invalid_params`: hand other schemes to the system (`/usr/bin/open`). The `bin/open` shim and `$BROWSER` in a terminal tile call this.

url.description: an absolute http or https URL

caller.description: the terminal the link comes from: the tile opens beside it; clients fill from EASL_TILE_ID

object.description: the browser tile showing the address

existing.description: a tile already showed the address: nothing was created

view.render.description: Render part of the board offscreen at a fixed scale, independent of the user's viewport (never moves it). `target` is an object id, a list of ids, or a board rect; ids render the board region under their outlines (with whatever overlaps them) and the whole route of every arrow between two of them, `full` draws those tiles' whole content (note/HTML scroll height; code: all of its range, scrolled to it and wrapped at its tile's width) extending below/right of their frames. Waits until content has painted (up to `timeoutMs`) and reports per-object state instead of returning blanks. App chrome (toolbar, tray, hints, selection rings, attention markers) is never drawn. A tile draws as on screen: its title bar at 1× (showing its content zoom's % when not 100%), its content at its `zoom` inside the frame.

scale.description: pixels per board point; lowered to keep the image under 32 megapixels (the result says what was used)

full.description: id targets: render the whole content, not just the part inside the frame

exclude.description: object types and/or object ids to leave out (e.g. ["terminal", "obj_…"]); a group id takes its members with it; targets are always drawn

padding.description: board points added around the target

out.description: absolute path to write; format from the extension (.png, .jpg/.jpeg). Clients resolve relative paths. Omitted: a new file under $TMPDIR/easl-renders/ (out of the repo)

inline.description: return the image in the reply (`data`, base64) and write no file: for a client on another machine, such as a remote board's viewer, which can't read the host's files. Doesn't combine with `out`

format.description: format of the temporary file, or of `data` with `inline`, when no `out` is given

timeoutMs.description: how long to wait for content (HTML pages, browser pages including loading one that isn't loaded, file reads) before drawing placeholders

path.description: absolute path written: `out`, or the temporary file; absent with `inline`

canvasRect.description: board area the image covers: pixel (px, py) = board (x + px / scale, y + py / scale)

scale.description: pixels per board point actually used

objects.description: every object drawn, bottom to top

view.snapshot.description: The board's window as the user sees it right now (viewport, tiles, toolbar, tray), with the viewport it shows. Terminal tiles are drawn from their session text. To look at something regardless of where the user is, use view.render.

out.description: absolute path to write; format from the extension (.png, .jpg/.jpeg). Clients resolve relative paths. Omitted: a new file under $TMPDIR/easl-renders/ (out of the repo)

format.description: format of the temporary file when no `out` is given

path.description: absolute path written: `out`, or the temporary file

scale.description: image pixels per board point (backing scale × zoom); the board fills the image from its top-left: pixel (px, py) = board (viewport.rect.x + px / scale, viewport.rect.y + py / scale)

objects.description: objects at least partly visible, bottom to top (state is always rendered)

session.spawn.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): start terminal tile `tile`'s zmx session, `canvas-<tile>`, on the machine easld runs on, as easld's own child, so the session and everything it runs stay in easld's cgroup (a hosted terminal's session: docs/contracts.md "Hosted terminals"). `command` runs in the user's login shell, which stays when it exits (`$SHELL -l -c '<command>; exec $SHELL -l'`); without one the session is the login shell. zmx keeps its sockets and logs in `<easld home>/zmx`, the user's own (a symlink, another user's directory or one others can write to is `unavailable`). A session that exists already is left as it is (`created: false`), unless one of its `canvas.home`, `canvas.board` and `canvas.tile` labels isn't the one `labels` gives (`conflict`, naming it). zmx's dead sessions (`status=cleaning up`) don't exist. Clients attach to it with `zmx attach canvas-<tile>` in that directory, once they have checked its labels.

tile.description: the terminal tile: the session is `canvas-<tile>`

command.description: argv run in the login shell; absent or empty: just the login shell

cwd.description: an existing directory on easld's machine (default: the user's home)

env.description: variables the session gets over easld's own environment (`EASL_SOCKET`, `EASL_TILE_ID`, `EASL_BOARD_ID`, …); `PATH` goes before easld's own

labels.description: zmx labels the session is created with (`canvas.board`, `canvas.tile`, `canvas.home`); keys and values in [A-Za-z0-9._-]

created.description: false: the session was already running

session.list.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): the terminal tiles' zmx sessions on easld's machine (`canvas-…`, whoever started them).

pid.description: the session's process (zmx's), absent while it doesn't answer

unreachable.description: zmx lists the session but it doesn't answer (its daemon stopped or wedged)

session.kill.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): end terminal tile `tile`'s zmx session on easld's machine and delete zmx's log of it. A session not labelled with `home` is left alone (`conflict`).

home.description: the caller's `canvas.home` label: only a session with this one is ended (without `home`, any)

killed.description: false: there was no such session

relay.open.description: easld only (the Mac app answers `unsupported`): serve a client's sockets to the programs on easld's machine, so a hosted terminal's integration and the `easl` CLI there reach the board that shows it (docs/contracts.md "Hosted terminals"). easld listens on `<home>/run/<instance>/easl.sock` and `cmux.sock` (the user's only) and passes each connection on to `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the client's ssh forward of a loopback port back to itself. Every user of the machine can reach that port, and anyone can listen on it once the forward is gone, so neither end sends the token: easld sends `<socket name> <nonce>`, the client's end answers `<nonce> <proof>` and easld `<proof>`, each proof the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the token, of `easl-relay <gate|easld> <socket name> <easld's nonce> <the client's nonce>`; nothing passes until both check. A connection the client's end doesn't take (refused, or no proof) closes at once, the integration spooling its report, and disarms the relay until the client opens it again. Opening it again with the same token takes the port; with a new one (the client's app restarted, or it reconnected) the sockets are bound anew at the same paths, so integrations watching them report again.

instance.description: the client instance, [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 64 characters

port.description: the loopback port the client's ssh forwards to it

token.description: 16–128 letters and digits: the secret both ends prove on every connection, new for each of the client's connections

easl.description: the socket for the easl API (a hosted terminal's `EASL_SOCKET`; integrations spool undelivered reports in `agent-reports/` beside it)

cmux.description: the socket for the cmux browser subset (`CMUX_SOCKET_PATH`)

opened.description: reports may have been spooled meanwhile (fetch and replay them): the sockets were bound now, or a disarmed relay re-armed; false for the same token and an armed relay

events.subscribe.description: Turn this connection into an event stream. Events: object.created, object.updated, object.deleted, tray.changed, agent.lifecycle, follow.updated, attention.changed ({id, active, message?, raisedBy?}).

client.attach.description: Make this connection a client that serves what only the Mac app can answer: the window (view.get, view.snapshot), drawing (view.render), live terminal surfaces (agent.prompt, agent.read's screen modes, agent.restart; interim: easld takes them over with zmx sessions, behind the same methods and errors), WebKit and language servers (object.reload), and AppKit text measurement (text.measure). A client built from an older schema `version` than the server's is refused `unavailable` ("easl 0.1.0 on studio is older than this board's server …; update it"); a newer one is accepted and speaks the server's `version` (the reply's), and with the same `version` the two work together whatever their `schema` hashes. Either way each uses what both know: params and `serves` names the server doesn't know are ignored. From then on the server sends this connection requests for the methods in `serves` (transport `clients`): a call that needs a client goes, after the server's own checks, to one that serves its method and shows its board (text.measure: any that serves it), the one whose user focused that board last, else the one focused most recently, else the one attached last. The call is forwarded as the same method with the caller's params (`board` and agent `target` resolved to ids; agent.prompt without `mentions`, which the server queues), and the client's result or error is the caller's. The server waits for object.reload's and view.render's `timeoutMs` plus 5 s and 30 s, else 5 s (view.get), 30 s (view.snapshot), 10 s (agent.prompt, agent.read, agent.restart), 2 s (text.measure); past that, or when the client disconnects first, the call fails `unavailable` (text.measure falls back to the glyph table). With no client for its board a delegated call fails `unavailable` saying what it needs. Attach again whenever `serves`, `boards` or `focused` change: each call replaces the last; closing the connection detaches. Answer text.measure without waiting on the server, which may hold a board while it measures. For the Mac app; agents never need it.

version.description: the schema `version` the client was built from: older than the server's is refused; a newer client speaks the server's (the reply's `version`)

schema.description: the client's schema hash: the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its schema/easl-api.json (generated: ApiParams.schemaHash)

app.description: the client's easl version, e.g. "0.2.0", for messages

host.description: the machine it runs on, for messages

serves.description: the methods this client answers: view.get, view.render, view.snapshot, agent.prompt, agent.read, agent.restart, object.reload, text.measure (others are ignored)

boards.description: the boards it shows (open in one of its windows or tabs), each open on the server; default none

focused.description: the board its user is looking at now (the key window's selected tab), one of `boards`; the client focused last on a board serves that board first

text.measure.description: Sizes of text as the board lays it out, in board points: an attached Mac client that serves text.measure (client.attach) measures it with AppKit, exactly as it draws; with none, or when it doesn't answer within 2 s, the server approximates from its glyph table (advance widths of the app's fonts, extracted on a Mac; no kerning) and says `approximate: true`. object.measure, `size: fit`, layout.check and arrow routing measure through it. note: `text` is markdown laid out as a note `width` wide (default 280) with its live fences and images read under `root`: the size is the note's whole frame (title bar included) and `tableShortfall` how much wider it would have to be to show every table cell whole; text: a text shape's text at `textSize` (default 1: 20 pt Shantell Sans) wrapped at `width` (default unwrapped): its bounds rounded up, plus 2; label: a rect's or ellipse's label (18 pt, centered) wrapped at `width`, likewise; arrowLabel: an arrow's caption (15 pt, centered, wrapped at 240): its chip, 8 wider than the text; caption: a code tile's caption strip (`inline code` in the code font): the narrowest frame that shows it whole, and the strip's height.

width.description: note: the frame's width (default 280); text and label: the wrap width (default unwrapped); ignored by arrowLabel and caption

root.description: note: the directory its fences' and images' paths are read under (default the board root)

board.description: the board whose root a note's paths default to

tableShortfall.description: note: points of width missing to show every table cell whole (0: nothing cut)

approximate.description: measured from the server's glyph table, not by a Mac client
